eligibility.evidence: Sec 3.1-3.2: three tasks (Tversky-Kahneman word-frequency item, Castello et al. modified item, Wason selection task) given to GPT-4o, Claude Sonnet 4, Gemini 2.5 Flash via API in three languages, with 169 human respondents.

A.title: Cross-linguistic patterns of cognitive biases in large language models: a comparative study in English, Hebrew, and Russian

paradigms.name: Original word frequency test (letter R in first vs third position; availability heuristic)
Modified word frequency test ('yes' vs 'no' more common; availability heuristic)
paradigms.source_paper: Castello et al. 2024 (inspired by Tversky & Kahneman 1974)

paradigms.name: Modified Wason selection task (airline passenger check-in, deontic framing; confirmation bias)

D.population: online convenience sample (Facebook groups, forums, SurveySwap), fluent in English, Hebrew or Russian; 58 English, 58 Hebrew, 53 Russian; highly educated
D.metric: proportion correct per task and language

E.headline: LLMs beat humans on the rule-based Wason task but showed human-like, model- and language-dependent errors on word-frequency tasks; accuracy varied significantly by prompt language.

G.notes: Single item per task and language (authors' limitation). Humans recruited by convenience, highly educated. Sec 4.2.2 text contradicts Table 2 for Gemini vs humans (English OWFT). Correctness keyed to corpus counts, not a normative rule, for the word tasks. LLM sessions are not independent samples. Correction note exists (10.3389/frai.2026.1925443), not read.
